_README: moroccoforamericans facts.json (schema_version 3) — RECONCILED across 4 sources (claude, gemini, deepseek, grok) via reconcile.mjs + manual dispute resolution. Agreed facts → agreed_stable. Material disputes on YMYL/safety fields (emergency numbers, currency export rule) were resolved against OFFICIAL sources and marked 'verified' with source_url — NOT by vote-counting (the majority was wrong on both). serve_live fields (exchange rate, flight prices, daily budgets) carry ranges as notes but value stays null — serve live, never frozen. Content stages read THIS file only.

locale.money_framing: Express costs in USD with MAD (dirham) equivalents. Dirham is a CLOSED currency — cannot be obtained before arrival; withdraw at ATMs on arrival or exchange USD locally.

type.note: US citizens visa-free up to 90 days (live web-confirmed 2026-08-12).

online_authorization_required.note: AEVM electronic authorization exists but does NOT currently apply to US/UK/EU visa-free travellers as of 2026-08-12. Morocco has signalled it may extend AEVM to visa-exempt countries in future — RE-VERIFY before each publish.

passport_validity_required.value: Official rule is more lenient, but airlines commonly enforce a 6-month rule; safe standard = passport valid at least 6 months beyond entry, with one blank page for the stamp.
passport_validity_required.note: Web-confirmed 2026-08-12: sources differ (Morocco official ~3 months vs airline-enforced 6 months); article uses the safe 6-month standard.

onward_ticket_required.value: Proof of onward/return travel may be requested at check-in or entry.

notes.value: Carry a passport copy; a blank page is needed for the entry stamp; proof of sufficient funds may occasionally be requested. Police checkpoints exist, especially near the Sahara.

approx_rate_note.notes: VOLATILE — serve live USD↔MAD. Roughly 1 USD ≈ 10 MAD historically but MUST be served live, never frozen.

cash_vs_card.value: Cash-heavy economy. Cards accepted at hotels, upscale restaurants, and modern city shops; souks, taxis, small cafes, and rural/desert areas are cash-only.

atm_availability.value: ATMs widespread in cities, towns, and at CMN/RAK airports — withdraw dirham on arrival (major banks: Attijariwafa, BMCE/Bank of Africa, Banque Populaire, CIH). Sparse in the deep Sahara; carry cash for desert legs.

currency_import_export_limit.value: MAD is a CLOSED currency: you cannot obtain it before arrival and cannot take more than 2,000 MAD out of the country (exceeding this is illegal, not just declarable). Foreign currency: no import limit, but amounts over the equivalent of 100,000 MAD must be declared to customs on arrival (form J7). Keep exchange receipts to reconvert leftover dirham to USD/EUR before departure.
currency_import_export_limit.notes: RESOLVED against IATA + Moroccan customs + Wise. Panel disagreed (1,000 vs 100,000 vs 'prohibited') — majority conflated the 2,000 MAD export cap with the 100,000 MAD foreign-currency declaration threshold. Both figures are real but apply to different things.

tipping_norm.value: Tipping expected but modest: ~10% in restaurants if no service charge, round up taxis, small tips (5–20 MAD) for guides, porters, and hammam staff.

intercity_rail.value: ONCF trains connect Casablanca, Rabat, Fez, Marrakech, Tangier; comfortable and punctual. Al Boraq high-speed line runs Tangier–Casablanca. Book first class for reserved seats. Note: NO train to Chefchaouen, Essaouira, or the Sahara.

buses.value: CTM and Supratours are the reliable intercity coach companies — used to reach Chefchaouen, Essaouira, and Sahara gateways not on the rail network. Book ahead in high season.

domestic_flights.value: Royal Air Maroc and low-cost carriers link major cities; usually unnecessary for the compact first-timer loop.

ride_sharing.value: Petit taxis (metered, in-city) and grand taxis (shared, intercity) are standard — insist on the meter or agree fare first. Ride-hail apps (Careem, Heetch, inDrive) operate in some larger cities.

car_rental_and_driving.value: Drive on the RIGHT. US license accepted for short stays (IDP recommended). Cities are chaotic and parking is hard; many first-timers hire a driver instead. Toll motorways connect major cities. Police checkpoints common; keep documents handy.
car_rental_and_driving.notes: Driving side right; BAC limit low (~0.02%) — verify. Avoid night driving in rural/mountain areas.

climate_by_season.value: Spring (Mar–May) and fall (Sep–Nov) are ideal: warm days, cool nights. Summer (Jun–Aug) is very hot inland (Marrakech, Fez, Sahara can exceed 100°F/38°C); coast (Essaouira) stays mild. Winter (Dec–Feb) is cool, Atlas gets snow, desert nights are cold.

advisory_level.value: US State Dept Level 2: Exercise Increased Caution (terrorism) — reported as of early-mid 2026. VERIFY current level + date before travel.

main_risk.value: Petty crime (pickpocketing, aggressive touts/faux guides, medina scams) and traffic — violent crime against tourists is rare. Morocco is generally considered safe, including for solo travelers, with normal precautions.

vaccines.value: No mandatory vaccines for US travelers arriving from the US. Routine vaccinations current; Hepatitis A and typhoid commonly recommended (food/water); consult a travel clinic or CDC.

tap_water_safe.value: Officially chlorinated in cities but commonly causes stomach upset for visitors — stick to bottled/filtered water; avoid ice from unknown sources.

emergency_numbers.notes: RESOLVED against multiple 2026 sources. Primary: 112 (universal from mobile) and 19 (police in cities); 177 Gendarmerie (rural/highway); 15 ambulance (SAMU); fire is 15 or 150 (civil protection). NOTE: 3 of 4 panel models said police='190' — that is a secondary/older listing; 19 and 112 are the current primary numbers. Vote-counting would have picked the wrong value.

sim_esim.value: Local SIMs (Maroc Telecom, Orange, Inwi) cheap with data-heavy tourist packages, sold at airports/shops (passport needed). eSIMs (Airalo etc.) let you land connected — good since the dirham is closed and you may want maps/rideshare immediately on arrival.

coverage.value: Strong 4G/5G in cities and along main routes; patchy to none in the deep Sahara and remote Atlas — download offline maps before desert legs.

costs._note: Approximate USD/day per person excluding international flights; serve_live-ish.

daily_budget_low.value: $40–70/day (riad dorms/budget guesthouses, street food, shared transport)

daily_budget_mid.value: $90–160/day (mid-range riad, mix of restaurants, some private transport/tours)

dress_norms.value: Morocco is a Muslim country; dress modestly especially outside tourist zones — shoulders and knees covered is respectful. Women aren't required to cover hair (except inside some religious sites, most of which are closed to non-Muslims). Cities like Marrakech are used to tourists; rural areas are more conservative. Lightweight, covering clothing also helps with sun and heat.
